text.p: A senior police official on Wednesday dismissed the idea that two Lithuanians arrested in Miami for allegedly trying to sell nuclear weapons could have access to such armaments and said they were simply swindlers.

The two Lithuanians, Alexander Progrebeshki and Alexander Darichev, were arrested in Miami earlier this week on charges of plotting to sell nuclear and other weapons to U.S. undercover agents posing as Colombian drug dealers.
"They are two small guys who tried to commit a swindle in the U.S., a very big swindle," said Aurelijus Racevichius, head of the Lithuanian branch of international police force Interpol.
"To my mind, they would have no chance to lay their hands on rockets or nuclear weapons," he told Reuters.
He said Progrebeshki was wanted in Lithuania but only in connection with a property fraud after he allegedly sold an apartment that did not belong to him.

The two Lithuanians pleaded not guilty before a federal magistrate on Monday on charges of conspiring to ship explosive materials and missiles without a licence and conspiring to unlawfully transfer nuclear materials.
According to an arrest affidavit, the two allegedly offered agents at meetings in Miami and London a shopping list of shoulder-fired and other surface-to-air missiles for sale.
The suspects said the weapons would be supplied by Armimex, a Bulgarian state-owned munitions supplier licensed by the former USSR to produce Soviet weapons during the Cold War.
The Bulgarian trade industry on Wednesday denied any wrongdoing in the case.
